paragraphs: Meadow makes software that handles the student financial experience at colleges, from application to graduation. The company says more than 300 higher education institutions use it.

One product is a net price calculator that gives prospective students a cost estimate in under three minutes. A billing product aims to cut manual work for staff and resolve balances sooner. A pre-collections product goes after unpaid tuition balances without punitive action. A checkout product collects non-tuition payments such as parking passes, lab fees, event costs and ID replacements.

One case study follows Tulsa Community College, which implemented the pre-collections product. The gap it addressed was the six-month period between the end of a semester and referral to traditional collections. Text messaging proved especially effective there for the college's dual enrollment population. Meadow also joined a Foundation for California Community Colleges procurement program to widen access to its tools among California community colleges and independent institutions. The founders trace the idea back to a bad higher education financial experience of their own.

quote.text: The mission is simple: empower students financially and strengthen economic mobility through higher education.
